application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description:
T1, Monterey pine, Reduce three protruding branches by up to 1.5m to balance the canopy
T2, London plane, Remove deadwood and assess for Massaria disease during works
T4, London plane, Remove deadwood and assess for Massaria disease during works
T11, Sycamore, Fell to ground level
T18, Common lime, Reduce canopy by 3m to approximately 25m height and 6m spread
T21, Tree of heaven, Fell to ground level
T24, London plane, Remove deadwood and check for Massaria disease
T25, London plane, Remove deadwood and check for Massaria disease
T26, London plane, Remove deadwood and check for Massaria disease
T28, Sweet chestnut, Reduce southwestern branch by up to 2m to reduce biomechanical stress
T29, Horse chestnut, Fell to ground level
T34, Hybrid poplar, Reduce canopy by 4m to alleviate biomechanical stresses
T38, Common hawthorn, Fell to ground level
T45, False acacia, Remove sub-dominant stem affected by cavity back to point of origin
T46, False acacia, Remove major deadwood and low-vigour branches to tidy crown
T47, Common lime, Re-pollard to established points
T74, Sycamore, Reduce canopy by up to 3m to reduce wind loading
T81, Sycamore, Remove broken branches and major deadwood
T87, Douglas fir, Remove broken branches and assess for split branches during works
T90, Wych elm, Remove major deadwood
T91, Common ash, Remove major deadwood
T92, Sycamore, Remove broken branch
T93, Sycamore, Sever ivy to 1.5m and remove major deadwood
T99, Weeping willow, Remove failed sections and reduce height by approximately 3m
T106, Norway maple, Fell to ground level
T115, Norway maple, Reduce canopy on southeast side by 2.5m to reduce wind loading
T120, Horse chestnut, Reduce canopy by 2.5m to reduce wind loading
T121, Norway maple, Reduce canopy by 2m to established growth points
G7, Sycamore and common ash group, Sever ivy to 1.5m and fell dead or heavily declining trees
G10, Mixed species group, Remove broken branches
H1, Western red cedar, Monitor condition and remove if decline persists or worsens
